Topic: The Third Condition of Mantra — How Tantra-Mantra-Y antra Kriya and Pitrus Stop You Fr om Pr ogr essing

Sour ce: A short Ashaeiynn Foundation training video (video transcript, ~17.5 min) — a dir ect instructional monologue rather than a live satsang Q&A. Continues the "Thr ee Conditions of Mantra" ar c first intr oduced in Session 14, now explaining Condition Thr ee in full mechanical detail: how black magic (tantra-mantra-yantra kriya) actually operates as a connectionbased science, how opportunistic wandering negativity attaches itself even without being deliberately sent, and how pitrus (deceased family members) specifically hold back a household's spiritual pr ogr ess. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on conversational content: this is a short, dir ect training monologue with no sangat back-and-forth — ther e is no separate curated conversational supplement for this session (see closing note).
1. WHY THIS TOPIC MATTERS

This session works thr ough Condition Three (freedom fr om tantra-mantra-yantra interfer ence and pitru interfer ence) hypothetically and mechanically , step by step , so a practitioner can genuinely understand — not just fear — how these obstacles actually function, and therefore how to eventually judge, clarify , and terminate them.
2. BLACK MAGIC IS FUNDAMENT ALLY A CONNECTION

Black magic (tantra-mantra-yantra kriya) is described as nothing mor e than a deliberately established CONNECTION between a target and the person performing the practice. This connection can be built in many ways: taking a physical part of the tar get (hair , nail clippings, a piece of clothing), or — modern tantriks having become considerably more advanced — simply using a name, or even a vehicle r egistration number . No specific physical item is strictly required. Once this connection is established, it becomes str ong enough that "pulling the string" fr om the tantrik's end pr oduces a felt effect on the target's end. Since the tantrik cannot act directly on the tar get themselves, they instead send a pr eta (spirit) to serve as an agent — essentially a spy — who ensur es the intended effect actually happens and continuously reports back to their "master ." This is described as a very old, lar gely unrecognized science, used in villages everywhere, which many practicing tantriks themselves don't fully understand the mechanics of, even while using it ef fectively in practice.
3. HOW THE SENT NEGATIVITY DRAWS ITS POWER

The negativity sent this way draws its power from TWO combined sour ces: continuously fr om the tantrik (thr ough the established connection), and additionally by draining the target's own body/energy whenever the target performs puja or jaap. This combination gives the sent entity considerable power to press down on and disturb the tar get. This produces a specific, counterintuitive pattern: the MORE such an affected person performs puja-paath, the MORE tired, weak, and generally worse they tend to become — because the negativity is feeding of f both the tantrik's ongoing

supply and the tar get's own generated ener gy simultaneously . A recognizable household example: an elderly woman who does a gr eat deal of puja-paath, yet develops pain acr oss seemingly every part of her body over time — this combined-feeding dynamic is of fered as a plausible explanation for that pattern.
4. HOW NEGATIVITY CAN ATTACH WITHOUT BEING DELIBERATELY SENT

A second, distinct scenario doesn't involve any tantrik at all. Many negativities — bhoot, pret, jinn, vaital, kinnar , pishach, and other subtle-body forms — simply roam freely , including in ordinary public places. If a practitioner doing jaap generates a daily surplus of energy , opportunistic wandering entities can notice this and quietly attach themselves , deliberately trying to remain undetected (since discovery would allow the practitioner to deal with them). Such an entity takes energy incr ementally and gradually , until enough has accumulated that the practitioner begins to feel something is wr ong : excessive tiredness after puja, a lack of any real results despite consistent ef fort, and an increase in negative or intrusive thoughts. This is offer ed as the explanation for why so many devoted, sincer e puja-paath practitioners end up among the unhappiest people — negativity attaches specifically because no proper protection is in place, not because the practice itself is wrong. An important r eframe: when this happens, the fault lies with the practitioner's own lack of pr otection and lack of drishti (spiritual sight) — not with any inher ent malice or special power of the negativity itself. As Bhaiya puts it plainly: if the fault were genuinely theirs, they would have been dealt with long ago; the real issues are that the practitioner cannot see what's happening (no drishti) and has no security in place — and this is exactly what opportunistic negativity exploits.
5. THE LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCE OF LEAVING THIS UNADDRESSED

Without addr essing this, a person's life can pass by with very little r eal spiritual gain — some small portion may arrive only after death, but by that point the attached negativity has often grown so powerful that the person's own subtle body , after death, ends up standing behind and serving that very same negativity , rather than the reverse. This has been dir ectly observed through drishti. A pointed observation on the general human condition: an ordinary small-time tantrik at a str eet corner often opens his own drishti first, while highly educated people (even PhD holders, driving expensive cars) fr equently never bother to pursue drishti at all , considering themselves too sophisticated for it — only to eventually end up going to that same streetcorner baba for help anyway , sometimes with further negative consequences if that baba then exploits the situation ("adhikar dete ho" — you grant them authority over you by asking).
6. HOW PITRUS SPECIFICALLY FORM AND BEHAVE

Example: if a grandfather passes away , he becomes a pitru for his family . If he still carried unresolved kaam, krodh, lobh, moh, mad, matsar (desire, anger , greed, attachment, pride, envy) at the time of death — which, per this teaching, is essentially guaranteed in the pr esent day given how widespr ead malinta (impurity) and vasana (desir e) have become — that pitru will likely try to "obsess"/attach within the family home after death, having no genuine spiritual practice or ener gy reserve of his own to draw on in his next stage of existence, and being surrounded by many other freely roaming pretas. A pointed, deliberately uncomfortable illustration: five elderly men chatting together will still look at women passing by — Bhaiya asks rhetorically whether such people, upon death, are somehow guaranteed to enter a purely devata-like state. The clear answer given is no — so after death, such unresolved tendencies can carry over into inappropriate interference within the pitru's own family , including with women in the household, since there is no longer anyone or anything to stop or restrain such behavior once the person has left the physical body . This is offer ed as the explanation for a r ecognizable symptom pattern: persistent pain in the feet, hands, or shoulders in some households (beyond what ordinary housework would explain), and elders in a household becoming noticeably

mor e quick to anger or difficult to r eason with than they pr eviously wer e — a genuine personality shift is treated as a meaningful sign that something is actively "turning" a person's mind, not merely an ordinary mood change.
7. HOW A HOUSEHOLD PITRU TRIES TO DOMINATE — AND WHY IT TARGETS SADHNA SPECIFICALLY

A pitru entrenched in a household will try to dominate it — covering up for or protecting a son, while causing trouble specifically for a daughter -in-law . Importantly , it will NOT try to stop the family's ongoing ritual puja-paath itself (continued bhog of ferings actually benefit the pitru, since it keeps being fed) — but it WILL actively try to stop anyone in the household fr om pursuing serious personal sadhna aimed at genuinely opening their own drishti. The reason: the pitru knows that if someone in the household succeeds at this deeper practice, that person's own dimension/power will eventually surpass the pitru's, and their opened drishti will expose everything the pitru has done — harassing family members, consuming the family's offerings, and so on. The pitru will therefor e covertly oppose that person, even trying to turn the r est of the household against them, specifically to get them to quit their sadhna. If the practitioner perseveres regardless, the pitru will eventually be defeated ("pitega hi pitega"). Pitrus ar e also sometimes deliberately "bound" and sent by tantriks to attack a specific target, particularly when ordinary negativity alone pr oves insufficient — this is described as a real, practically used technique, to be covered in more depth in future live Zoom sessions.
8. WHY DRISHTI CANNOT OPEN UNTIL THESE ARE FULLY REMOVED

A practitioner's drishti cannot genuinely open until all such negativities ar e removed, all pitrus ar e removed, and all forms of tantric interfer ence ar e fully ended. Once drishti has genuinely opened, these three specific obstacles (tantramantra-yantra interference, opportunistic negativity , and pitru interference) are described as never being able to trouble that person again.
9. WHAT ASHAEIYNN OFFERS TO ADDRESS THIS

Hawan (fir e ritual) is pr esented as the primary , fastest method for removing this kind of negativity . Ashaeiynn has conducted hawan daily , without interruption, for the past three years, and anyone can join. This is described as a fast pr ocess, though it carries an associated cost. A free alternative exists: the "deepak" (lamp) pr ocess, alr eady explained by mentors, which is entir ely fr ee of cost — though it takes longer to achieve the same r esult. The underlying principle: a practitioner must give either time or cost — one of the two is r equired, and ther e's no way ar ound pr oviding at least one. Until these obstacles ar e genuinely r emoved, further spiritual pr ogr ess remains blocked — this closes out the "Three Conditions of Mantra" teaching arc that began in Session 14.

1. Black magic (tantra-mantra-yantra kriya) is fundamentally a deliberately established connection between a tar get and a practitioner — built through a physical item, a name, or even a vehicle number , not necessarily requiring a physical object. 2. A tantrik sends a preta as an agent/spy through this connection to ensure the intended ef fect happens and to report back — this negativity draws power both from the tantrik and by draining the tar get's own generated ener gy during puja/jaap. 3. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 23, English)
The Third Condition of Mantra — How Tantra-Mantra-Y antra Kriya and Pitrus Stop You From Pr ogr essing
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation training module. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. What actually IS black magic (tantra-mantra-yantra kriya) — how does it r eally work? A: Jai Siya Ram! At its core, it's nothing more than a deliberately established connection between a tar get and the person performing the practice. This connection can be built through a physical part of the tar get — hair , nail clippings, a piece of clothing — but modern tantriks have gotten far more advanced, and now often just need a name or even a vehicle registration number . No specific physical item is strictly required once a connection is set up.

Q2. If ther e's a "connection," how does the tantrik actually affect me fr om a distance? A: Once the connection is strong enough, "pulling the string" from the tantrik's end produces a felt ef fect on the tar get's end. Since the tantrik can't act on the tar get directly themselves, they send a preta (spirit) as an agent — essentially a spy — to ensure the ef fect happens and to continuously report back to their "master ." This is described as a very old, lar gely unrecognized science, used in villages everywhere, that even many practicing tantriks don't fully understand mechanically despite using it ef fectively .

Q3. I do a lot of puja and jaap but keep getting mor e tired and unwell instead of better — why? A: This is a specific, recognizable pattern this teaching addresses. If negativity has been sent your way , it draws power from two combined sources: continuously from the tantrik through the established connection, and additionally by draining your own body/ener gy whenever you perform puja or jaap. That combination gives the sent entity real power to press down on and disturb you — so the more such an affected person does puja-paath, the more tired and weak they tend to become, since the negativity feeds of f both sources at once. A recognizable household example given is an elderly woman who does a great deal of puja-paath yet develops pain across seemingly every part of her body over time.

Q4. Does negativity only come fr om someone deliberately targeting me, like a tantrik sending it? A: No — there's a second, distinct scenario that doesn't involve any tantrik at all. Many negativities (bhoot, pret, jinn, vaital, kinnar , pishach, and other subtlebody forms) simply roam freely , including in ordinary public places. If a practitioner doing jaap generates a daily surplus of ener gy , opportunistic wandering entities can notice this and quietly attach themselves, deliberately staying undetected since discovery would allow the practitioner to deal with them.

Q5. How would I even know if something like that had attached to me? A: It takes ener gy incrementally and gradually until enough has accumulated that you begin to feel something is wrong: excessive tiredness after puja, a lack of any real results despite consistent effort, and an increase in negative or intrusive thoughts. This is of fered as the explanation for why so many devoted, sincere puja-paath practitioners end up among the unhappiest people — the negativity attaches specifically because no proper protection is in place, not because the practice itself is wrong.

Q6. If this happens to a sincer e practitioner , is it their fault somehow? Did they do something wr ong spiritually? A: The fault isn't malice or wrongdoing on the practitioner's part — it lies specifically in their own lack of protection and lack of drishti (spiritual

sight). As Bhaiya puts it plainly: if the fault were genuinely theirs in some deeper sense, they would have been dealt with long ago. The real issues are that the practitioner cannot see what's happening (no drishti) and has no security in place — and that's exactly what opportunistic negativity exploits.

Q7. What happens if I never addr ess this kind of interfer ence in my lifetime? A: Without addressing it, a person's life can pass with very little real spiritual gain — some small portion may arrive only after death, but by then the attached negativity has often grown so powerful that the person's own subtle body , after death, ends up standing behind and serving that very same negativity rather than the reverse. This has been directly observed through drishti.

Q8. Why do highly educated, successful people sometimes end up at some random r oadside baba for help? A: This teaching makes a pointed observation: an ordinary small-time tantrik at a street corner often opens his own drishti first, while highly educated people (even PhD holders, driving expensive cars) frequently never bother pursuing drishti at all, considering themselves too sophisticated for it — only to eventually end up going to that same street-corner baba anyway , sometimes with further negative consequences, since asking for help that way can grant that baba real authority ("adhikar") over them.

Q9. What exactly is a "pitru," and how does one form? A: A pitru is a deceased family member who becomes attached to the family after death. The example given: if a grandfather passes away , he becomes a pitru for his family . If he still carried unresolved kaam, krodh, lobh, moh, mad, matsar (desire, anger , greed, attachment, pride, envy) at the time of death — which, per this teaching, is essentially guaranteed today given how widespread impurity (malinta) and desire (vasana) have become — that pitru will likely try to "obsess"/attach within the family home, since he has no genuine spiritual practice or ener gy reserve of his own in his next stage of existence, and is surrounded by many other freely roaming pretas.

Q10. Isn't it uncomfortable to suggest a deceased r elative might behave inappr opriately after death? A: This teaching addresses that discomfort directly with a pointed illustration: five elderly men chatting together will still look at women passing by — so are such people somehow guaranteed to enter a purely devata-like state the moment they die? The answer given is no. So after death, unresolved tendencies can carry over into inappropriate interference within the pitru's own family , including with women in the household, since there's no longer anyone or anything to stop or restrain that behavior once the person has left the physical body .

Q1 1. Are there any warning signs that a household might have an entr enched pitru? A: Yes — a recognizable symptom pattern includes persistent pain in the feet, hands, or shoulders in some households (beyond what ordinary housework would explain), and elders in the household becoming noticeably more quick to anger or dif ficult to reason with than they previously were. A genuine personality shift is treated as a meaningful sign that something is actively "turning" a person's mind, not merely an ordinary mood change.

Q12. If a pitru is in our home, will it stop us fr om doing our regular puja and rituals? A: No — it will NOT try to stop the family's ongoing ritual puja-paath itself, since continued bhog of ferings actually benefit the pitru by keeping it fed. What it WILL actively try to stop is anyone in the household pursuing serious personal sadhna aimed at genuinely opening their own drishti.

Q13. Why would a pitru specifically target someone's personal sadhna instead of the family's rituals? A: The pitru knows that if someone in the household succeeds at deeper practice, that person's own dimension/power will eventually surpass the pitru's, and their opened drishti will expose everything the pitru has done — harassing family members, consuming the family's of ferings, and so on. So the pitru will covertly oppose that person, even trying to turn the rest of the household against them, specifically to get them to quit. If the practitioner perseveres regardless, the pitru will eventually be defeated ("pitega hi pitega").

Q14. Can a tantrik use a pitru as a weapon against someone, not just ordinary negativity? A: Yes — pitrus are also sometimes deliberately "bound" and sent by tantriks to attack a specific tar get, particularly when ordinary negativity alone proves insuf ficient. This is described as a real, practically used technique, to be covered in more depth in future live Zoom sessions.

Q15. Why can't my drishti open if I still have this kind of interfer ence ar ound me? A: A practitioner's drishti cannot genuinely open until all such negativities are removed, all pitrus are removed, and all forms of tantric interference are fully ended. But once

drishti has genuinely opened, these three specific obstacles — tantra-mantra-yantra interference, opportunistic negativity , and pitru interference — are described as never being able to trouble that person again.

Q16. What does Ashaeiynn actually offer to deal with all of this? A: Hawan (fire ritual) is presented as the primary , fastest method for removing this kind of negativity — Ashaeiynn has conducted hawan daily , without interruption, for the past three years, and anyone can join. It's fast, but it carries an associated cost. A free alternative exists too: the "deepak" (lamp) process, already explained by mentors, which is entirely free of cost, though it takes longer to achieve the same result.

Q17. Is ther e really no fr ee, fast way to handle this — do I always have to pay or wait? A: The underlying principle taught here is that a practitioner must give either time or cost — one of the two is required, and there's no way around providing at least one. The daily hawan is fast but paid; the deepak process is free but slower . Until these obstacles are genuinely removed through one path or the other , further spiritual progress remains blocked.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 23 additions)

If a user asks why they feel worse the more puja/jaap they do, explain the combined-feeding mechanism (tantrik's connection + draining the tar get's own ener gy) rather than suggesting the practice itself is at fault. If a user describes symptoms like persistent unexplained pain, growing fatigue after spiritual practice, or a family elder becoming noticeably more short-tempered, gently introduce the pitru/opportunistic-negativity framework as a possible lens — without asserting a definite diagnosis about their specific situation, since this teaching frames such things as verifiable only through opened drishti. Frame the "fault lies with lack of drishti/protection, not the practitioner's wrongdoing" reframe explicitly when discussing why sincere, devoted practitioners sometimes suf fer — this avoids implying spiritual failure or shame on the user's part. When explaining pitru interference, keep the register measured and non-alarming, especially regarding the sensitive point about interference with women in a household — present it as this teaching's explanation of a mechanism, not as a claim about any specific real person's deceased relative. If a user asks about remedies, present both the daily hawan (fast, paid) and the deepak process (free, slower) evenhandedly , using the "either time or cost" framing rather than pushing one option over the other . Do not overstate what has been taught on binding/sending pitrus via tantriks — this session explicitly defers deeper detail to future live Zoom sessions.
